title: Commutative Coarse-graining on the Sphere
authors: Chayut Teeraratkul, Hussein Aluie
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26896v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Filtering by spatial convolution underlies coarse-graining and Large Eddy Simulation, the analysis of multiscale dynamics, and data processing across the sciences. Yet, as commonly practiced on the sphere, it violates a basic consistency requirement: commutation with differential operators, which is necessary for deriving coarse-grained dynamics and preserving the physics across lengthscales. We discuss the root of the problem, which is intrinsic to the curved geometry rather than being a result of metric terms, coordinate system, or numerical grid. A recently proposed generalized spherical convolution is, for a given scalar kernel, the unique linear operator commuting with the radial projection, divergence, and curl. Any consistent linear operator, be it spectral truncation, wavelet transform, diffusion, Green's-function inversion, or a machine-learned convolution, necessarily takes this form. From a simulation of an unstable jet, we demonstrate commutation to within numerical round-off, whereas common filtering that ignores curvature produces significant spurious divergence where none exists and gradient errors comparable to the gradients themselves.

title: Concurrent Entanglement Purification Scheduling in Dynamic Quantum Networks
authors: Gongyu Ni, Lester Ho
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum networks must deliver end-to-end entanglement whose fidelity meets application requirements, which typically requires entanglement purification along multi-hop paths. Existing scheduling approaches either purify at the link level or optimize end-to-end fidelity for a static set of requests, and do not capture concurrent requests competing for network resources over time. This paper studies concurrent entanglement purification scheduling in a time-slotted quantum network with heterogeneous links, in which requests compete for link capacity and quantum memories, and each request may be served by multiple parallel paths for increased reliability. We formulate a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) scheduler that maximizes the number of scheduled requests, with max-min path allocation as a fairness criterion, and develop reinforcement learning (RL) schedulers based on DQN, PPO, and SAC, whose rewards balance request success against Bell-pair consumption. Simulations under varying network load, topologies and target fidelity thresholds show that the RL schedulers achieve the highest success rates, improving on MILP by up to 6% and on Progressive Filling and Greedy heuristics by 16.5% and 19.5% respectively, at the cost of higher Bell pair consumption and the deferral of a small fraction of requests. MILP, in contrast, achieves the highest fairness and the lowest Bell pair consumption in most scenarios.

title: Symmetry and Quantum Interference in the Attosecond Domain
authors: C. Figueira de Morisson Faria, S. Hashim, J. Rivera-Dean, T. Rook
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.

title: Enhancing analytical photon transport in turbid media through physics-guided neural network corrections
authors: Guojun Tang, Paul D. Teal, Alexander Doronin
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26917v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Analytical methods provide rapid and computationally efficient predictions of light transport in turbid media, making them attractive for real-time and inverse applications. However, their accuracy is limited by the approximations and assumptions used to obtain tractable solutions. On the other hand, Monte Carlo (MC) simulation is widely regarded as the "gold standard" for modeling light transport in turbid media, but its high computational cost limits its use in applications requiring repeated forward evaluations. Here, we introduce a physics-guided residual learning framework that combines the computational efficiency of analytical modeling with the accuracy of MC simulation. As a representative case study, we consider the diffusion approximation (DA), which can exhibit systematic errors under relatively strong absorption, weak scattering, and imperfect boundary treatment. Given the absorption coefficient, scattering coefficient, and anisotropy factor, the corresponding DA prediction is incorporated as a physical prior, while the network learns only the residual between the analytical prediction and the MC reference. Across the evaluated optical-property range, the proposed framework reduces scalar-reflectance RMSE and spatially resolved reflectance RMSLE by factors of approximately 62 and 14, respectively, relative to the diffusion approximation. With only 1\% of the available training data, it achieves approximately 87\% and 93\% lower corresponding errors than a direct neural-network surrogate. These results demonstrate that learning corrections to an analytical physical baseline improves both prediction accuracy and data efficiency.

title: Matrix-Free Resolvent Analysis for Large-Scale Aerodynamic Systems
authors: Rohit Sunil Kanchi, Sicheng He
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26931v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: At industrial scale the cost of resolvent analysis is set by the linear solves and the assembly and storage of the Jacobian. We present a matrix-free resolvent framework in the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes solver ADflow: automatic differentiation supplies the action of the shifted Jacobian and its Hermitian transpose, preconditioned Krylov solves recycle subspaces across a Lanczos bidiagonalization, and every gain is certified by a backward error. It is applied to the NASA Common Research Model wing at Mach 0.85 and 4.2 degrees on three grid levels of 0.45, 3.6 and 28.8 million cells, the finest with 1.73x10^8 complex unknowns, 2.3 times the largest reported resolvent computation. On the coarsest level an unstable buffet mode makes the gain peak a resonance; on the finer two the operator is stable and the peak, 1.33x10^4 at omega = 6.4 and 3.0x10^3 near omega = 7.7, is a pseudo-resonance of damped modes whose buffet cells travel outboard at about 0.3 times the free-stream speed. Refinement turns an oscillator into an amplifier of the same mechanism, as forced simulations confirm. A certified frequency costs 3.6 minutes on 128 cores at 2.7 million unknowns, with 14 to 34 kB per unknown, nearly four orders of magnitude below a sparse factorization.

title: Phase-dependent THz yield in two-color laser plasmas: nonlinear propagation and Coulomb-modified recollision
authors: Yange Chen, Ahai Chen, Jiahui Guo, Tianmin Yan, Yizhu Zhang, Yuhai Jiang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26939v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Two-color laser-induced plasmas provide a reliable source of broadband terahertz (THz) radiation and offer several control parameters for optimizing THz yields. We investigate the phase-dependent THz yield (PTY) driven by a two-color laser field with parallel linear polarizations, using a model that couples macroscopic nonlinear propagation and microscopic Coulomb effects. Comparisons with models accounting for either effect alone show that their coupled effects shift the yield extrema and reshape the phase-dependent response. Nonlinear propagation distorts the local laser waveform, while the Coulomb interaction modifies the subsequent electron dynamics, particularly recollision. These changes modify the directional asymmetry of the photoelectron momentum distribution and hence the THz emission. Within the studied range, the combined model predicts a larger shift of the optimal phase than either effect alone, together with a reduced phase separation between the yield maximum and its adjacent minimum. These findings may guide THz optimization with more complex driving fields.

title: Gerchberg-Saxton Optimized Silicon Metasurface for Sinusoidal Structured-Light Three-Dimensional Imaging
authors: Gengyuan Ye, Shuming Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26956v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) optical imaging based on structured illumination has attracted considerable attention in applications including machine vision, robotics, and computational sensing. However, conventional structured-light systems generally rely on bulky projection components, such as digital micromirror devices and diffractive optical elements, which limit system miniaturization and integration. Here, we demonstrate a compact structured-light 3D imaging platform enabled by a silicon dielectric metasurface operating at a near-infrared wavelength of 940 nm. The desired sinusoidal fringe illumination is encoded into the metasurface through a Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) phase optimization algorithm, which converts the target far-field distribution into a nanoscale phase profile and subsequently into silicon nanopillar geometries. The fabricated metasurface generates high-quality sinusoidal structured illumination, which is integrated with a four-step phase-shifting reconstruction method to recover 3D object profiles. The proposed approach provides a compact and scalable solution for miniaturized structured-light projection and optical 3D sensing.

title: FoundPDE: A generative foundation model for data-driven symbolic discovery of partial differential equations
authors: Langchen Liu, Junlin Luo, Min Zhu, Zhuoran Yang, Lu Lu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discovering governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from observed data is a central inverse problem in computational science and engineering: the goal is not only to predict trajectories, but to identify interpretable symbolic laws that can be analyzed and reused. Existing PDE discovery methods often depend on hand-designed libraries, accurate numerical derivatives, or per-equation symbolic search, making them fragile under sparse observations, noisy data, broad equation families, and unseen symbolic compositions. Here, we introduce FoundPDE, a pretrained data-to-symbol foundation model for PDE discovery. FoundPDE maps discretized spatio-temporal trajectories to symbolic equations with a transformer, uses Fourier and first-order spatial-derivative augmentation to expose complementary trajectory information, refines numerical coefficients, and supports downstream extension with improved generalization through few-shot fine-tuning and hierarchical discovery. On a clean in-domain benchmark spanning 20 PDE families, our model reaches 97.50% type recognition. Under coefficient shifts beyond the training support, type recognition remains 90.53%; under multiplicative Gaussian noise on the model input, it is 94.43% at a 2% noise level but falls to 52.09% at 10%. For unseen composite equations, few-shot fine-tuning reaches over 90% exact recovery on four held-out families, and we further develop a hierarchical discovery algorithm that recovers two-term composites without fine-tuning FoundPDE. By amortizing symbolic discovery across equation families, FoundPDE shifts PDE discovery from per-dataset search toward a reusable pretrained model that extends to new physics with limited additional data, a step toward foundation models that uncover interpretable governing laws directly from scientific data.

title: Punctuated Equilibrium in Technological Capabilities: Commercial Selection and the Predictability of Frontier Advances
authors: Kenzi M'Hamdi, Dawoon Jeong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolutionary accounts of technological change connect new technical opportunities with economic selection. Using approximately 1.74 million electronic-component product records, we examine the tempo of capability-frontier improvement alongside the diversity of commercially offered products. In a detailed analysis of 29 manually selected capabilities, 77.8% of substantial-advance episodes consist of a single observed advance year. Across eligible three-year windows beginning with an advance, the initial observed gain accounts for an average of 79.3% of total log-capability improvement. The median share of product records near the frontier is 1.46%. Motivated by the interaction of technology push and demand pull, we extend the analysis to 204 capabilities and conduct forward out-of-sample comparisons between models using frontier history and models additionally incorporating product composition, manufacturer competition, and population dynamics. The additional indicators do not improve forecasts of subsequent frontier advances. The results document concentrated frontier gains alongside a broad distribution of commercially offered specifications. Stylized comparisons of incremental service value and switching costs identify candidate mechanisms linking application-specific valuation and production scale to the economic relevance of technical opportunities. They also specify the price, quantity, and application-level observations needed to evaluate these interpretations. We propose source-grounded, language-model-assisted extraction of demand-related information from dated external documents, with validation against independently observed market data.

title: Anchored Exploration in Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework for Semiconductor Designs
authors: Huy Nguyen, Dawoon Jeong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26973v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.

title: Load-Balanced Neural-Network-Aided Adaptive Tabulation of Phase Equilibria for Transcritical Multiphase Flows
authors: Navneeth Srinivasan, Po-Yu Lai, Suo Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.26984v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulating high-pressure transcritical flows with phase change is critical for advanced propulsion, yet traditional first-principles approaches, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) calculations, consume most of the runtime and frequently fail to converge. Standalone machine learning models introduce heavy evaluation overhead across large grids, while dynamic tabulation still relies on fragile iterative solvers. To resolve these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid In-Situ Adaptive Tabulation and Artificial Neural Network (ISAT-ANN) framework. A pre-trained ANN replaces the iterative solver during table expansion to guarantee crash-free operation, while ISAT enables rapid data retrieval via local linear interpolation. To eliminate parallel load imbalances, an O(N) greedy load-balancing algorithm redistributes computational tasks across cores. Coupled with Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR), the framework was validated on a Mach 5 shock-droplet interaction benchmark. It accurately captured shock-interface dynamics without instability, achieving a 2.30 times speedup in thermodynamic calculations on a single core and 2.62 times in parallel over standalone ANNs, with AMR providing an additional 2.92 times overall efficiency boost. This plug-and-play framework offers a stable, scalable path for high-fidelity multiphase flow simulations.

title: Shaping the spectra of second harmonic laser by spatial focusing
authors: Yan-Ming Liu, Tao Xie, Xiangying Hao, Rui-Bo Jin
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurately controlling the spectral width of second harmonic generation (SHG) is critical in applications such as nonlinear microscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and quantum optics, where tailored spectral properties are required. Although it is known that the focal length of the lens used to focus the pump beam influences the SHG spectrum, a simple and precise theoretical understanding of this effect has been lacking. Here, we develop a theoretical model to describe how pump focusing conditions affect SHG spectral broadening, and experimentally validate the model using BBO crystals with lenses of 50 mm and 200 mm focal lengths. Our results establish a practical method for engineering the SHG spectral width through pump focusing, providing valuable guidance for designing nonlinear optical systems with specific spectral requirements.

title: A Geometric Principle for Path Selection in Directed Acyclic Graphs
authors: Haya AlMuhanna, Tim S. Evans
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There are many types of path between nodes of a Directed acyclic graph (DAG), including the shortest and longest paths. Here, we ask whether the choice of path used in any analysis reflects the geometry of the latent space in which the DAG is embedded. To do this we define L_p-cube spacetimes, a family of continuous ordered spaces in which a single parameter p determines whether the ordered distance satisfies the ordered triangle identity when p>1, or the reverse ordered triangle identity when 0

<1 or p<0, both of which are rarely studied. The forward connection kernel in the p<0 case has infinite hyper-volume, yet it is a well defined model. We then construct random geometric DAGs embedded in our L_p-cube spacetime and study their geometry. For p>1, where the ordered triangle identity holds, the shortest paths provide the closest approximation to the continuum ordered geodesic while for 0

<1 and p<0, where the reverse ordered triangle identity holds, this role is instead taken by the longest weighted path. We also test the robustness of this relationship in a geometric citation model in which the random geometric DAG is supplemented by a preferential-attachment-type mechanism allowing connections beyond the strict geometric cut-off. The same broad correspondence between latent geometry and ordered geodesic path type is recovered. Our results show that the preference for shortest or longest paths in a DAG is closely connected to the geometry assumed for its latent space, and suggest that path structure can provide information about latent geometry, even when that geometry is not directly observed.

title: Parallel Omnidirectional Atom Rearrangement with Dynamic Holograms
authors: Samuel A. Engel, Dewei Gong, Ziguang Lin, Lysander Christakis, Kang-Kuen Ni, Norman Y. Yao
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27053v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The ability to assemble and reconfigure individual atoms is central to performing quantum science using optical tweezer arrays. Here, we demonstrate parallel omnidirectional atom transport and rearrangement using dynamic holograms generated by a single kilohertz-rate spatial light modulator. By carefully characterizing survival and heating, we show that atoms remain confined even when successive holograms are commanded before the liquid crystal has settled, enabling significantly faster transport. To generate holograms in real time, we develop and implement a warm-start, weighted Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm that achieves performance comparable to neural-network methods without requiring any training. Combining these techniques, we assemble ytterbium atoms into a 2078-site kagome lattice with 99.0% mean filling. In addition, we demonstrate parallel transport between array layers, combining axial and transverse motion to reconfigure atoms in three dimensions. Our approach is readily adaptable to existing tweezer platforms and provides a method for large-scale SLM-based atom assembly as well as programmable three-dimensional control.

title: Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
authors: Till Bargheer, Tengis Batmunkh, Paul Ryan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27062v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.

title: Polynomial-Time Classical Simulation of BosonSampling under Any Constant-Fraction Photon Loss
authors: Byeongseon Go, Hyunseok Jeong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27065v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding how photon loss changes the classical complexity of BosonSampling is central to assessing the robustness of near-term photonic quantum advantage. In this work, we present a polynomial-time classical simulation algorithm for lossy BosonSampling that applies whenever a constant fraction of the input photons survives. We consider the standard fixed-loss model, where $N$ input photons propagate through an $M$-mode interferometer and exactly $N-n$ photons are lost uniformly at random, leaving $n$ surviving photons at the output. For any constant surviving fraction $n/N\in(0,1)$, the algorithm samples from a distribution within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the fixed-loss BosonSampling distribution with probability at least $1-\delta$ over Haar-random interferometers, in time $\operatorname{poly}(M,N,\varepsilon^{-1},\delta^{-1})$. We further extend the fixed-loss analysis to the uniform-transmission-loss model and obtain analogous polynomial-time simulability for any fixed transmission rate $\eta\in(0,1)$. These results substantially extend the known provably simulable regime of $n=O(\sqrt{\varepsilon N})$ surviving photons or $\eta=O(\sqrt{\varepsilon/N})$ transmission rate, and demonstrate that even the experimentally relevant linear-survival regime can admit efficient classical simulation under the conditions considered here.

title: Cavity models of non-Abelian gauge theories
authors: Lucia Valor, Jacquelin Luneau, Klaus Liegener, Stefan Filipp, Peter Rabl
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27070v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In quantum optics and related fields, cavity quantum electrodynamics provides a powerful framework for modeling the low-energy properties of bound charges coupled to electromagnetic fields, using a minimal set of atomic levels and isolated photonic modes. Here, we develop a similar framework for non-Abelian gauge theories, focusing on the pure-gauge dynamics of SU(2) fields as the conceptually simplest example. Starting from the corresponding Yang-Mills Lagrangian, we derive an SU(2) cavity Hamiltonian in the Coulomb gauge, represented in terms of only three localized bosonic modes. Unlike its non-interacting electromagnetic counterpart, this model exhibits a nontrivial excitation spectrum featuring bound composite gauge particles ('glueballs') as the lowest-energy configurations. We extend this framework to one-dimensional arrays of coupled SU(2) cavities and discuss the driven excitation of a glueball condensate and the clustering of multi-glueball states as two elementary interaction-induced processes in these models. These examples offer a glimpse into the multitude of novel many-body phenomena that arise within this cavity SU(2) framework and we show how this physics at the interface between particle physics and quantum optics can be experimentally explored using state-of-the-art superconducting quantum circuits.

title: R\'enyi multi-entropy of graph states and the $n -> 1$ limit
authors: Sriram Akella, Abhijit Gadde
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27080v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: R\'enyi multi-entropy extends the R\'enyi entropy to pure states of more than two parties. It is defined by a replica contraction at integer replica number $n$, and the multi-entropy is its $n\to1$ limit. In holography this limit is conjectured to compute the area of a minimal soap-film web in the bulk. Understanding multi-entropy for general states, however, is harder. Unlike the bipartite case, the replica contraction is not a moment of a density matrix, and the continuation to $n=1$ has to be found by other means. We study this problem for qubit graph states. We show that at every odd $n$ the contraction equals $2^{-k/2}$, where $k$ is a sum of ranks of matrices over a finite field, one row and one column per qubit. We define a class of graphs that we call collision-controlled, for which the rank sum is a polynomial in $n$. This class includes graphs without even cycles and all complete bipartite graphs. The natural polynomial $n \to 1$ continuation is a finite sum over partitions of the parties. While the R\'enyi multi-entropy is non-increasing under single-qubit Pauli measurements at every odd integer $n>1$, the continuation to $n=1$ is not. A $Z$ measurement on one qubit of an odd ring with $2r + 1 \geq 7$ qubits raises it from $(r+1)\log 2$ to $(2r-1) \log 2$. Thus the continuation is not an entanglement monotone.

title: Active isolation of transmon readout with a tunable inductive bridge
authors: Chunyang Ding, Chuyao Tong, Paul Varosy, Nikitha Jain, Ziyi Zhao, Eric I. Rosenthal, Konrad W. Lehnert, David I. Schuster
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27137v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scalable superconducting quantum computation requires fast, high-fidelity readout. Currently, this is assisted through cryogenic amplification of the readout signal. In traditional dispersive readout schemes, the amplifiers that are used to provide high signal-to-noise ratio also generate thermal noise that can decohere the qubits, demanding additional ferrite-based isolators to suppress this noise. Here, we integrate a chip-scale microwave switch, the tunable inductive bridge, into the readout chain of a fixed-frequency transmon. Flux-pulsing the switch, such that it transmits only during the readout, did not make a discernable difference to qubit coherence, residual excited-state population, or readout fidelity metrics. By injecting broadband noise that mimics amplifier thermal photons, we show that the switch suppresses the resulting qubit dephasing by more than $30$~dB, consistent with its independently measured on-off ratio, establishing it as a potential chip-based integrated replacement for readout-chain isolators.

title: Allight: A Perfect Photon Collector
authors: Dan Porat, Ran Finkelstein, Tal Carmon
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27161v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Collecting photons from quantum emitters remains a key limitation in light-matter interaction because conventional lenses collect light only from one direction. Here, we introduce a perfect light collector by inverse-designing a surrounding dielectric structure that encloses the emitter to increase photon-collection efficiency toward unity. Decomposing the device into several refractive interfaces enables emission collection from the full 4$\pi$ solid angle with adiabatic reshaping into a collimated beam. We experimentally demonstrate, in two dimensions, the ray bending that collimates omnidirectional emission. Our collector transforms current paradigms for highly efficient photon collection from narrowband, cavity-based techniques into experimentally robust, broadband, non-resonant dielectric devices.

title: The next phase of quantum energy science: from mechanisms to applications
authors: Florian Metzler, Matt K. Lilley, Matthew C. DeCapua, Peter L. Hagelstein, Jonah F. Messinger, Nicola Galvanetto
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A growing research community spanning quantum batteries, molecular and excitonic energy transport, polaritonics, quantum materials and nuclear control has begun to describe its work in terms of quantum energy or quantum energy science. What connects these otherwise disparate efforts is the deliberate use of quantum states, couplings, collective effects and engineered environments to control energetic states and pathways. A key difference from quantum information science is that the complete quantum state does not always need to be preserved; engineered dissipation or dephasing can even improve the desired outcome. We organize this emerging domain through a framework that connects mechanisms, functions, capabilities, and applications. We identify five elementary functions (Excite, Hold, Release, Transfer, and Transform) and examine the mechanisms that implement them. The same functions recur from the molecular to the nuclear scale, although their relative implementation difficulty can differ sharply. Moving toward technology, we highlight three engineering capabilities (Storage, Routing, and Conversion) through the performance metrics that matter for their applications. Stretch scenarios illustrate what performance targets could make these capabilities technologically consequential.

title: Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope
authors: Conrad Silio, Cristian Staii
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27167v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.

title: Comparative Optical Spectroscopy of Er$^{3+}$, Tm$^{3+}$, and Eu$^{3+}$ Molecular Complexes at Cryogenic Temperature
authors: Farhad Rasekh,  Sahil, Arsalan Mansourzadeh, Diogo Alves G\'alico, David Hunger, Muralee Murugesu, Daniel Oblak
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27223v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rare-earth molecular complexes are attracting increasing interest for quantum information applications because of their structural flexibility and chemical tunability. Here, we compare the cryogenic optical properties of Er$^{3+}$, Tm$^{3+}$, and Eu$^{3+}$ complexes in the same ligand environment. Optical spectroscopy shows differing behavior across the three systems: spectral hole burning is observed in the Eu$^{3+}$ complex, whereas no measurable hole is detected in the Er$^{3+}$ and Tm$^{3+}$ complexes. We measure laser-induced local heating and rethermalization in the Er$^{3+}$ and Tm$^{3+}$ powder-like samples, observing strong local heating and slow thermal relaxation in the cold-plate cryostat. The recovery occurs over several seconds and, for some Er$^{3+}$ excitation conditions, extends over tens of seconds. The comparison across the three ions nevertheless suggests that heating alone is unlikely to account for the full contrast. Rather, the different behaviors of Eu$^{3+}$, Tm$^{3+}$, and Er$^{3+}$ point to ion-dependent relaxation and decoherence processes associated with their electronic level structure and coupling to the molecular environment. Temperature-dependent linewidth and line-shift measurements are further consistent with phonon-mediated broadening through coupling to crystal-field levels.

title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
authors: Lawrence M. Qin, Sky Semone, Matthew J. Brandsema, Christos Argyropoulos
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27226v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.

title: The optical force on a dielectric slab
authors: Andrew Laeuger, Kevin Kuns, Yanbei Chen, Nancy Aggarwal
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Radiation-pressure forces on transmissive optics, including dynamical backaction, are usually computed from the momentum flux of the external fields. For a dielectric of finite thickness, this omits the time dependence of the electromagnetic momentum stored inside. We compute the force on a lossless dielectric slab of arbitrary thickness $L_s$ submerged in a dielectric fluid, proceeding from both Lorentz force on its bound charges and from the external momentum fluxes for arbitrary carrier and sideband fields. We treat the surrounding medium through a prescribed linear dielectric response and do not model the accompanying mechanical response of the fluid, including pressure and electrostriction. These two methods both recover the expected force in the limit of a thin reflector, but differ in the more general case by the rate of change of the field momentum stored in the slab. This storage term vanishes for static fields and at low frequencies reduces to $(L_s/c^2)\,dP/dt$, where $P$ is the net power through the slab. In a cavity, where $P$ depends on the slab position, the storage term produces a velocity-dependent force. The Abraham and Minkowski momentum formulations applied to the storage term are reconciled to give an unambiguous force on the dielectric in the case of an exterior vacuum environment, where there is no fluid response to model.

title: Optimal four-copy detection of the three-tangle and its fault-tolerant cost
authors: Federico Tom\'as B. P\'erez, Berta Casas, I-Chi Chen, Su Yeon Chang, Philipp Schleich, M. Cerezo
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27260v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The three-tangle, $\tau_3$, is a measure of genuine tripartite entanglement that distinguishes GHZ-type from W-type entanglement in pure three-qubit states. Here, we identify the statistically optimal one-sided four-copy detector of the three-tangle and study its implementation cost. The optimal detector has click probability $\tau_3^2/48$, while previous four-copy constructions achieve $\tau_3^2/256$ and therefore require asymptotically $16/3$ times as many experimental repetitions. Using the representation-theoretic structure of the problem, we construct an ancilla-free implementation of the optimal detector using 15 CNOT gates, together with an 11-CNOT detector with click probability $\tau_3^2/96$. These results reveal a tradeoff between statistical efficiency and implementation cost, since reducing the number of repetitions requires increasingly expensive circuits. We then show that this tradeoff persists once the circuits are encoded. In a fully fault-tolerant setting, the increased click probability comes with a substantial non-Clifford synthesis cost, while an early fault-tolerant implementation based on $T$ gates and STAR rotations reduces this overhead at the expense of additional encoded resources. We quantify these costs using both the Steane and $[[8,3,2]]$ codes, providing explicit resource estimates for implementing the optimal detector across different computational regimes.

title: Analytical solution of electromagnetic heating in a stratified absorbing medium
authors: Ulises Jaime-Yepez, Hongyun Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27274v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider the temperature evolution in a skin tissue when it is exposed to an electromagnetic wave. The heating is caused by the absorbed power as the electromagnetic wave attenuates inside the skin. In many applications, the characteristic depth of attenuation is small in comparison with the lateral size of the electromagnetic beam. Because of this separation of length scales, the lateral heat conduction is negligible at leading order. Previously, we studied electromagnetic heating in a skin of a single homogeneous layer. We derived the leading-term analytical solution and the asymptotic corrections up to the second order for lateral heat conduction and for oblique incidence. In this study, we derive the analytical solution in the case of perpendicular incidence on a stratified skin tissue with a layer-specific profile for electromagnetic attenuation. It should be emphasized that in the current study, the heat capacity and conductivity are still uniform over the entire skin tissue; only the electromagnetic attenuation is stratified resulting in a layer-specific heating profile.

title: Time-resolved Rydberg dynamics in molecules
authors: Erfan Saydanzad, Van-Hung Hoang, Uwe Thumm
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27286v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a general theoretical framework for the ultrafast dynamics of coherently populated autoionizing Rydberg states in molecules, whose coherent decay results in asymmetric Fano line shapes produced by interference between resonant autoionization and direct ionization. The asymmetric line shapes form in the photoelectron continuum during the autoionization lifetime of the decreasing Rydberg population. By parameterizing autoionization resonances and solving the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation, we model the buildup of the Fano profile together with the decline of the coherently excited Rydberg-state population. We compare our calculated photoelectron yields with the XUV-pump--IR-probe photoemission experiment of Biswas et al., Phys. Rev. A 110, 043106 (2024), in which neutral ground-state CO$_2$ molecules are excited by an XUV pulse to the Henning sharp and diffuse Rydberg series and subsequently ionized by the delayed IR pulse. Based on our numerically modeled photoelectron yields, we analyze two complementary processes: (i) photoemission into the $X^2\Pi_g$ continuum of residual CO$_2^+$ ions, which exposes interferences between direct photoionization and excited-state autoionization, and (ii) IR-induced photoemission into the CO$_2^+$[$B^2\Sigma_u^+$] continuum, which reveals quantum beats between Rydberg states. Our close-coupling model provides a versatile, extendable framework for tracking molecular Rydberg-state relaxation and, more generally, light-driven coherent dynamics in complex quantum systems.

title: Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture
authors: Andre Laestadius, Mih\'aly A. Csirik
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27294v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.

title: District Size Matters: How Seats Per District Shapes Proportionality Under STV
authors: Daryl DeFord, Thomas Ratliff, Ellen Veomett
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27297v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the impact of utilizing multimember districts and Single Transferable Vote (STV) as the winner selection method on partisan proportionality. We start with detailed case studies of the upper legislative houses of Illinois, New Hampshire, and New Mexico, building ensembles of redistricting maps with mostly 2-member, mostly 3-member, and mostly 4-member districts for each state. These ensembles are constructed using two methods: building from precincts, and merging currently existing single-member districts. We also compare two ballot generation models for each experiment: a modified Bradley-Terry model and a Plackett-Luce model. We find that our ensembles of multimember districts paired with STV have results which are centered closer to partisan proportionality than when single member districts are used. However, the choice of district size affects partisan outcomes enough that this choice could be exploited by a partisan mapmaker to advantage a particular party. The findings are consistent across all combinations of district construction and ballot generation models within a single state. We then expand our study to 41 different states, obtaining consistently similar proportionality results and allowing us to empirically evaluate the two ballot generation models, as implemented in VoteKit, at a national scale.

title: Machine-learned spectral PDE solvers for fluids and plasmas
authors: Mellow Baixuan Chen, Alan A. Kaptanoglu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27317v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse regression methods for discovering governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from data are sensitive to observation noise and are not constrained to reproduce the data under forward integration. We address both limitations by performing weak-form discovery in the spatial discretization in which the PDE is solved, learned by differentiating through multistep rollouts anchored at the observed states. The new method, Weak-form Anchored Rollout for PDEs (WARP), produces a machine-learned PDE solver. In this work, we focus on systems amenable to a spectral Galerkin solver. Across eight benchmark fluid and plasma systems, including high-dimensional turbulent simulations, WARP produces numerically stable rollouts from new random initial conditions and substantially improves coefficient recovery, rollout accuracy, and statistical measures compared with a single-step weak-form SINDy baseline.

title: Shot Allocation Strategies in Debugging Quantum Circuits
authors: Era Thaqi, Coco Gong, Margaret Martonosi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27335v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Debugging quantum programs remains challenging due to the nature of quantum measurement. As quantum algorithms and systems scale, it is increasingly crucial to develop rigorous debugging and verification approaches. Statistical assertion-based debugging validates quantum program behavior through repeated circuit execution and statistical hypothesis testing, but existing frameworks treat shot count as a fixed input parameter, leaving the problem of optimal shot allocation across multiple mid-circuit assertions unexplored. To improve debugging efficiency by making better use of given shot counts, this paper proposes and evaluates four shot allocation strategies within the QDB quantum debugger implemented within the CUDA-Q framework. These allocation approaches: equal split, static weight allocation, adaptive entropy routing, and sequential retirement, use statistical approaches to test whether qubits have expected state characteristics at different points in execution. We evaluate these allocation strategies on different circuits, under both noise-free and depolarizing noise conditions. We show how adaptive strategies use shots efficiently by concentrating them on assertions with high uncertainty. This substantially reduces total shot usage while maintaining comparable debugging confidence.

title: Assignment maps for arbitrary reduced quantum dynamics
authors: James Fullwood, Weixiang Ye
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27338v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Given an open quantum system $S$ with environment $E$, we establish a one-to-one correspondence between completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) maps from $S$ to $E$ and assignment maps initializing the composite system $SE$ in a possibly correlated state prior to unitary evolution. We show that every possible joint state $\rho_{SE}$ can be realized by such assignment maps, which are inherently Hermiticity-preserving and trace-preserving (HPTP). While these maps sacrifice global positivity, we derive a simple necessary and sufficient condition for any local state of $S$ to belong to their domain of validity. Furthermore, we prove that the geometry of this domain is governed by the joint state assigned to the maximally mixed input, ensuring that a non-zero volume of admissible local states can readily coexist with initial system-environment entanglement. Finally, we provide an operational protocol for witnessing such limits of validity.

title: Continuous and Differentiable Neural Network Representations of the Surfzone Sea-Surface from Lidar Point Clouds
authors: David R. Culver, Matthias Morzfeld, Falk Feddersen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27352v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ocean waves are often analyzed via sea-surface observations. Multi-beam scanning lidar enables two-dimensional measurements of the water surface $\eta(x,y)$ via sequenced point clouds of sea-surface elevation. Point cloud data, however, have to be gridded, interpolated, or mapped for use in wave analysis. We present and test a method for creating a continuous and differentiable (space and time), but grid-free, representation of the sea-surface from time sequenced lidar point clouds. We use a specific neural network architecture, a SIREN, to represent the sea-surface and to train the network on spatiotemporal 60~s of lidar data collected by a gas-electric UAS (drone) hovering over large (4 m), breaking waves in Monterey, California. The trained SIREN allows estimation of the sea-surface and its derivatives at any location and time. SIREN sea-surface representations tend to filter the highest wave number variability (splash-up and sea-spray). SIREN errors are comparable to instrument errors and insensitive to local data density. The reliability and reproducibility of our approach is tested by training two SIRENs independently on the same data. Differences between the two independent SIRENs are comparable to instrument error, but increase in data-poor regions. SIRENs' potential for directional wave analysis is demonstrated by computing spatial and temporal derivatives and by estimating wave velocity from a SIREN-generated space-time slice of the sea-surface.

title: Two routes to the Hadamard condition
authors: Eleanor March
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27359v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In quantum field theory on curved spacetime, the Hadamard condition is often presented as a necessary condition on 'physically reasonable', 'vacuum-like' states of linear quantum fields, and plays a central role in many theoretical and foundational applications - ranging from proofs of the renormalizability of Wick polynomials to derivations of the Hawking temperature. In this paper, I strengthen, generalise, and bring under technical control two popular motivations for the Hadamard condition - one which appeals to the role of Hadamard states in defining physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator on general curved spacetime backgrounds, and one which appeals to the equivalence principle. This clarifies the role and status of the Hadamard condition, including its relationship to the equivalence principle, to well-definedness of physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator, and the sense in which Hadamard states are 'vacuum-like'.

title: Choi-Jamio{\l}kowski isomorphism(s) and channel/state duality, naturally!
authors: Paul E. Lammert
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27394v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Provided a maximally entangled state vector in ${\mathcal{H}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$, the Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism of quantum information theory (or channel/state duality) produces a mapping of ${\mathsf CP}({\mathcal{H}},{\mathcal{K}})$ (completely positive maps of density operators on ${\mathcal{H}}$ tothose on ${\mathcal{K}}$) onto the density operators on ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$, which extends to a unitary map. Here, ${\mathcal{H}}$ and ${\mathcal{K}}$ are {finite-dimensional} Hilbert spaces.The nature of this construction, the form of the associated formulas, and the possibility of versions which do not require an entangled vector seed, are illuminated from the perspective of {naturality}, in the sense of Eilenberg and MacLane.There is a unique such correspondence (``Choi map'') natural in both ${\mathcal{H}}$ and ${\mathcal{K}}$ which produces density operators on either ${\mathsf L}({\mathcal{H}},{\mathcal{K}})$ (Hilbert-Schmidt inner product) or ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}^*$ instead of ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$. In particular, no entangled state input is required. There are no such binatural maps carried on ${\mathcal{K}}\otimes{\mathcal{H}}$, but those natural in only ${\mathcal{K}}$ are canonically associated with unitary maps ${\mathcal{H}}\rightarrow{\mathcal{H}}^*$ and derive from the binatural maps. The construction recovers the standard Choi-Jamiolkowski formulae and shows how they express naturality.

title: Quantum algorithm for high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equations based on Carleman linearization
authors: Koichi Miyamoto
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27416v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Addressing nonlinear numerical problems in quantum computing remains challenging, but several approaches, including Carleman linearization (CL), have been proposed to construct quantum algorithms for such problems. In this work, we develop a CL-based method for a high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equation (SDE) $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{X}_t = \left(A(t) \mathbf{X}_t + F(t) \mathbf{X}_t^{\otimes s}\right) \mathrm{d} t + B(t) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{W}_t$ for an $\mathbb{R}^N$-valued random process $\mathbf{X}_t$, aiming at quantum speed-up with respect to the dimension $N$. We introduce auxiliary processes $\mathbf{Y}^j_t$ that approximate $\mathbf{X}_t^{\otimes j}$, derive a linearized system of SDEs for them, and obtain the linear ordinary differential equation (ODE) governing their expectations. We then apply a quantum ODE solver to it and, from the resulting quantum state, extract an estimate for the expectation of a linear function of $\mathbf{X}_t$ by overlap estimation. We show that, provided the nonlinear and noise terms in the SDE are sufficiently small relative to the linear term, the CL error decreases exponentially with the truncation order $J$ in CL, and we can estimate the target expectation with a ${\rm polylog}(N)$ number of queries to unitaries encoding coefficient matrices $A$, $F$, and $B$. Finally, we also run a numerical demonstration for an SDE related to Langevin dynamics, observing the exponential decay of the CL error as $J$ increases.

title: Field demonstration of a self-contained 10 km mobile-to-ground quantum network node via common-aperture co-propagation
authors: Dongkyu Kim, Dong-Gil Im, Kyungdeuk Park, Jisu Kim, Jonguk Choi, Yonggi Jo, Yong Sup Ihn
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a dual-function, common-aperture free-space optical system that simultaneously supports decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution (QKD) at 803 nm and bidirectional classical laser communication at 640/660 nm over a 10.31 km terrestrial link from a mobile platform to a stationary ground station. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first field demonstration of a fully integrated common-aperture architecture where a co-propagating classical optical link simultaneously performs full QKD post-processing and ecrypted payload transmission over a 10 km atmospheric channel. The classical link utilizes Manchester-coded on-off keying (MC-OOK) at 10 MHz, achieving a packet error rate of $\sim$ 0.4 $\%$ (estimated bit error rate (BER) of 3.13 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$) with hardware-based self-synchronization and error-packet retransmission. Over the 10.31 km link, the QKD system achieved an average quantum bit error rate (QBER) of 2.512 $\%$ and an average secret key rate of 644 bps using rate-adaptive low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Finally, using the distilled keys, real-time AES-256 encrypted image transmission was executed over the co-aligned classical optical channel, proving the feasibility of a completely self-contained, jam resistant mobile quantum optical network.

title: Systematic Truncated Wigner Approximation for Open Spin Systems Reveals Long-Range Order Far from Equilibrium
authors: Igor Timofeev, Dawid A. Hryniuk, Marzena H. Szyma\'nska
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27462v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-range interactions can protect dissipative order against fluctuations, but determining when they do so in two dimensions remains out of reach for existing many-body methods. We develop a continuous SU(2)-covariant truncated-Wigner framework that maps the problem onto stochastic dynamics with one Bloch sphere per site. Derived systematically from the exact Stratonovich-Weyl evolution of the Lindblad equation, it generates both drift and reservoir noise for arbitrary spin $S$. Benchmarks against exact and tensor-network calculations validate its description of non-equilibrium dynamics and steady states. Applied to 400-site two-dimensional dissipative anisotropic XY lattices, our method reveals physics missed by mean-field and perturbative approaches: vortex-antivortex proliferation destroys the predicted staggered-XY phase for nearest-neighbour coupling, whereas algebraically decaying interactions stabilize an extended $\mathbb{Z}_2$-ordered phase. We obtain the first beyond-mean-field steady-state phase diagram of the long-range interacting model, revealing reentrant loss of order at strong coupling and closure of the ordered region beyond $\alpha\approx 3.5$. Our new method provides a scalable route to strongly correlated driven-dissipative systems with long-range interactions, higher-dimensional geometries, spin-boson couplings, and spins beyond one half, relevant to modern experiments with magnetic atoms and polar molecules in optical lattices and tweezer arrays.

title: Engineering \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two remote superconducting qubits via a multimode waveguide
authors: Da-Wei Wang, Yu-xi Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27471v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Waveguides provide a flexible platform for long-range interactions between superconducting qubits. Here, we study how to engineer the effective \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two qubits via qubit frequency assignments and multimode interference determined by the mode configuration and standing-wave parities of a finite multimode waveguide. For a single-mode waveguide, we find that \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions cannot be simultaneously suppressed to zero and the residual qubit-qubit coupling always exists. For example, the \(XY\) interaction may be suppressed to a negligible level when two qubits and the waveguide mode satisfy the two-photon resonant condition, but the \(ZZ\) interaction cannot be switched off. For multimode configurations within the central dispersive window, the engineered interaction types are very different for odd and even numbers of modes. Even-mode configurations can readily produce strong \(XY\) interactions, whereas odd-mode configurations can strongly suppress the \(XY\) interaction while retaining a finite \(ZZ\) interaction. Full-Hamiltonian simulations of minimal two- and three-mode configurations confirm \(XY\)-dominated SWAP dynamics and \(ZZ\)-dominated CZ-type dynamics, respectively. These results establish a frequency assignment criterion of qubits and waveguide modes for selectively engineering long-range qubit-qubit interaction types induced by the waveguide with finite multimode.

title: Quantum Cryptanalysis on Two Feistel-Type Constructions
authors: Yan-Ying Zhu, Bin-Bin Cai, Fei Gao, Song Lin
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27506v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing, the security of traditional cryptographic systems is facing significant challenges. As a fundamental component of symmetric cryptography, block ciphers have attracted increasing attention regarding their quantum security in recent years.
  In this paper, we propose new quantum attacks on two Feistel-type constructions, i.e., New Structure IV and the lightweight block cipher LBlock, under the quantum chosen-plaintext attack (qCPA) model. First, we construct an 8-round quantum distinguisher for New Structure IV and perform an $r(r>12)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. Compared with Li et al.'s qCPA-based result presented at INSCRYPT 2024, our attack reduces the time complexity by a factor of $2^{n/2}$, where $n$ denotes the subkey length. Second, we design a 9-round quantum distinguisher for LBlock and extend it to an $r(r>15)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. The proposed quantum distinguisher covers one more round than Liu et al.'s automated-search distinguisher at ASIACRYPT 2025, which results in a $2^{16}$ reduction in the time complexity of our $r$-round quantum key-recovery attack on LBlock. Furthermore, by analyzing the structure of the round function and the key scheduling of LBlock, we reduce the subkey guess space for the 15-round attack from 76 bits to 52 bits, lowering the time complexity from \(O(2^{38})\) to \(O(2^{26})\) by a factor of \(2^{12}\).

title: Collision-aware Bayesian mitigation of photon loss in linear optical quantum circuits
authors: Seungwoo Kim, Seunghyun Ahn, Donguk Nam, Hyunho Cha, Jungwoo Lee
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Photon loss is the dominant noise source in linear optical quantum circuits. Each lost photon turns an ideal n-photon outcome into a pattern with fewer photons, so the detector counts no longer follow the ideal output distribution, and the lossless events that do follow it become exponentially rare as the photon number grows. Discarding the lossy events (postselection) therefore wastes most of the data at realistic loss rates, and the ideal distribution has to be inferred from the lossy counts themselves. Recycling-based mitigation (Mills & Mezher, Quantum 2026; Quandela's photon_recycling) reweights lossy samples to recover lossless probabilities, but its estimators are biased and restricted to the no-collision sector, where each output mode holds at most one photon. We instead treat the raw counts as Multinomial observations under per-photon binomial loss and infer the ideal output distribution and the loss rate jointly from a Bayesian posterior, which extends naturally to outputs with collisions. On data from the independent Perceval simulator at the scale of prior work (n=4 photons in m=20 and m=10 modes), the posterior has lower KL divergence than both recycling and postselection at every tested loss rate in the no-collision benchmark. In the collision regime it recovers the loss rate and the collision-pattern probabilities, which recycling cannot estimate, and stays below recycling at every loss rate and below postselection except at low loss, where the two are comparable. Its advantage over recycling grows with the sample count, and it supplies credible intervals that the baselines lack.

title: Low-nonlinearity advantage of hollow-core fiber for wavelength multiplexing of quantum entanglement and classical DWDM signals
authors: Hikaru Shimizu, Arisa Ohno, Mao Miyasugi, Yumeno Seki, Naoyuki Funaoka, Yukari Takada, Aruto Hosaka, Shun Fujii, Hiroyuki Tsuda, Masahiro Takeoka
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27540v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coexistence of classical and quantum light in optical fiber is a key requirement for scalable quantum networks. However, it is fundamentally limited by nonlinear crosstalk from intense classical signals. Hollow-core fiber (HCF), with its intrinsically low optical nonlinearity, offers a promising solution. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the coexistence of polarization-entangled photons with dense wavelength-division multiplexed (DWDM) classical signals with a total launch power of 11.2 dBm, and perform a direct comparison between equal-length single-mode fiber (SMF) and photonic-bandgap-based HCF deployed in a campus network. We observe that HCF suppresses background noise by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to SMF, while preserving high-fidelity entanglement distribution. Our results provide clear experimental evidence of the advantage of HCF and establish its potential as a transmission medium.

title: Hybrid Lattice Surgery between Smooth Boundaries
authors: Grace Ding, Yanzhu Chen, Sheng-Jie Huang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27556v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop smooth hybrid lattice surgery for group surface codes, enabling joint logical measurements through merge and split operations along smooth boundaries. The code patches may correspond to identical or different finite groups, including non-Abelian groups. Our central result is that smooth merge and split realize a logical $K$-coset measurement, where $K$ is the subgroup defining the interface. This generalizes the joint logical parity measurement of ordinary surface codes. Using a tensor-network representation, we derive explicit measurement circuits and develop procedures for correcting nonidentity measurement outcomes. We illustrate the framework through a generalized controlled multiplication gate between group surface codes and protocols for preparing the $T$, $CZ$, $CCX$, and $CS$ magic states, producing resources encoded in one or more $\mathbb{Z}_2$ surface code patches. Our results show how smooth hybrid lattice surgery broadens the range of logical operations available for group surface codes.

title: Microscopic Bipartition and Macroscopic Symmetry in a R\'enyi Entanglement Ensemble
authors: Zhe Wang, Dongxu Liu, Zheng Yan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27587v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Universal information extracted from entanglement at a critical point is commonly associated with the long-distance properties of the bulk state, while microscopic details of a lattice bipartition are expected to be washed out under coarse graining. Counterintuitively, we show directly that such microscopic information can survive in the statistical ensemble that determines the second R\'enyi entropy and obviously change the physics there. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the square-lattice $J$-$Q_3$ model at the N\'eel--valence-bond-solid (VBS) transition, we measure magnetic and dimer order parameters in the R\'enyi-2 ensemble. For a standard axis-aligned bipartition, the VBS component perpendicular to the entanglement boundary remains finite in the thermodynamic extrapolation and is inequivalent to the parallel component, while the N\'eel order vanishes. For a $45^\circ$ tilted bipartition, in contrast, the two VBS components remain equivalent within numerical accuracy. We interpret this contrast in terms of the R\'enyi twist defect: the two bipartitions have the same bulk theory but realize different microscopic defect symmetries. Our results demonstrate that lattice information invisible to the bulk continuum theory alone can remain active in the long-distance R\'enyi ensemble, providing a microscopic explanation for the strong bipartition dependence previously observed in entanglement studies of deconfined criticality.

title: Fate of Discrete Time Crystals in Finite-Size Cavity QED Systems
authors: Haimi Nguyen, David R. Reichman
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27589v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: It has been shown that Discrete Time Crystal (DTC) behavior may arise in the periodically driven, open Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit ($N \rightarrow \infty$). In this work, we demonstrate that finite $N$ non-mean-field fluctuations in this model can lead to decay rates and amplitudes of transient DTCs that display a non-trivial non-monotonic behavior with an increasing number of atoms. We show that the second-order cumulant expansion fails to capture the finite-size dynamics, while a stochastic version of the Truncated Wigner Approximation (TWA) is remarkably accurate, particularly in the large atom ensemble limit. Using the TWA and the Monte Carlo Wave Function (MCWF) approach, we identify three distinct dynamical regimes of transient DTC behavior in the finite-size Dicke model. We outline the mechanism behind the non-monotonic finite size dynamical decay of DTC order and discuss the implications for experiments performed on finite-sized atomic assemblies.

title: Stabilizer R\'enyi moments beyond entanglement
authors: Vishnu Jejjala, Joydeep Naskar
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stabilizer R\'enyi moments depend on a choice of operator basis and need not be determined by entanglement spectra. In this paper, we study their spatial decay in critical quantum chains described by two-dimensional conformal field theories. We derive an exact entanglement baseline for reductions of pure stabilizer states and a symmetry selection rule for the charged contribution at fixed support. An exact Ising example shows that an on-site rotation changes the full decay exponent while preserving every subsystem entanglement spectrum. For growing Ising intervals at index two, we obtain an exact Pfaffian representation and compare the charged amplitude with a candidate conformal boundary calculation. The data support this prediction, but its identification with the lattice limit still requires endpoint matching and control of the order of limits.

title: Resolving Nonlocal State Reduction via Induced Coherence in Frequency-Comb Biphoton Sources
authors: Tai Hyun Yoon
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27602v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How macroscopic definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations emerge from entangled superpositions across spacelike-separated regions without superluminal action or {\it ad hoc} wavefunction collapse remains a defining open question in the foundations of quantum mechanics. Here, we resolve this century-long paradox within \textit{linear} relativistic quantum electrodynamics by developing an open-system and measurement-defined framework realized in dual, spacelike-separated nonlinear crystals driven synchronously by a multi-mode optical frequency comb and seeded by an ultra-narrow coherent laser. Expanding the transverse electromagnetic vector potential into discrete single-photon frequency-comb supermodes, we show that tracing out the unmeasured continuous-wave idler field yields an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation whose decoherence rate is governed by the non-orthogonal state overlap of single-photon-added coherent states. Connecting this open-system map to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory, we demonstrate that single-particle interference arises from the geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than remote collapse, establishing strict operational equivalence across pump, seed, and signal phase scans. The resulting wave-particle-entanglement triality equality $P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$ is saturated across the complete parameter space, while the atomic-clock-referenced comb structure anchors continuous-variable time-frequency displacement stabilizers directly at the hardware layer. Our work unifies induced coherence, Bohr's complementarity, and quotient measurement theory, providing a microscopic pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum information processing.

title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
authors: Tai Hyun Yoon
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27639v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $\pi$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.

title: Nanophotonic Extreme Ultraviolet Polarimeter
authors: Anna Kulter, Lorenz Wei{\ss}, David J. Grafinger, Alexander Sagar Grossek, Rodolfo Previdi, Martin Schultze, Marcus Ossiander
abstract:
arXiv:2610.27705v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. With a 0.9{\deg}-sensitivity for polarization rotations in a 1-second measurement and single-shot capability, the device opens new experimental opportunities in ultrafast magneto-optic spectroscopy and at accelerator-based light sources.
